card.intuition: Early in a session an agent sits in a smart zone — sharp, focused, with good recall — and as the session grows it drifts into a dumb zone with more mistakes and faithfulness hallucinations. Same model and harness, just more context. The decline is gradual and commonly begins around 125K-150K tokens on frontier models, and the practical budget for a task is the tokens the agent works well within, not the window limit it can technically hold.
card.analogy: A consultant who is freshest at the Monday-morning kickoff and progressively duller by Friday afternoon on the same engagement — same consultant, just accumulated context and fatigue. Unrelated work spends the budget, so book one engagement per sprint and hand off at natural boundaries rather than pushing through.
card.time_complexity: O(C squared) per request over the full context window — the quadratic pairing arithmetic under the smart zone means deeper context costs more per request even as quality falls, so planning around the smart zone keeps both in a working band.
card.space_complexity: Context/memory footprint: every token in the window spends the finite attention budget, and unrelated work spends the zone, so one task per session keeps the footprint small and the work sharp.
when_to_use: Planning around the smart zone, not the window: size tasks to the tokens the agent works well within
Running one task per session so each starts in the sharpest part of the session
Splitting a task bigger than one smart zone: hand off or compact at a natural boundary and resume in a fresh session
Reading the signs: forgets an instruction from twenty turns ago, repeats a corrected mistake, or asserts something the context contradicts
gotchas: The zones do not track the context-window limit — quality falls off long before the harness refuses to continue
Pushing through and re-explaining adds more context and makes the slide worse
The decline is smooth and easy to miss: there is no error message and no visible boundary

steps.label: Fresh session
steps.annotation: Early in a session recall is good, focus is high, and mistakes are rare.

steps.label: Tokens accumulate
steps.annotation: Each completed task burns tokens, so starting a second task in the same session starts it closer to the dumb zone.

steps.label: Slide into the dumb zone
steps.annotation: On frontier models quality commonly falls off around 125K-150K tokens, though the exact number is debated.

steps.label: Signs of the slide
steps.annotation: The agent forgets an instruction from twenty turns ago and confidently asserts things the context contradicts.

steps.label: Window still has room
steps.annotation: The session can be deep in the dumb zone with most of the window free; quality falls off long before the limit.

steps.label: Reset at a boundary
steps.annotation: Compact or hand off at a natural boundary and let a fresh session start the next piece inside the smart zone.

exercise.prompt: Plan a task against the smart zone: return how many fresh sessions it needs when the practical budget is the zone size.
hints: Each session runs inside the zone budget; bigger tasks need more sessions.
Divide the task size by the zone budget to count extra sessions beyond the first.
exercise.test_code:
assert sessions_needed(60_000, 130_000) == 1
assert sessions_needed(160_000, 130_000) == 2
assert sessions_needed(300_000, 130_000) == 3
